title: Three Years and One Short Bib
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：target　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 target 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the athlete ① set the target that no trainer in the stadium would have measured, and he said the setting was the whole of the year. The ② target, meaning the mark itself and not the bib, ran three years and stayed unmeasured in the book; a target, he said, is the only thing in a stadium that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ target in that stadium had the same short bib beside it, and the ④ target at the far track, meaning the lap they kept for the children to count and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A target, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the athlete said the measuring is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the target was the whole of the matter, meaning the aim and not the mark. The ⑥ target, meaning the aim and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; target, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a mark and an aim. He said the aim is the part they remember.

By 1994 the ⑦ target had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short bib. The ⑧ target of the whole thing, the athlete wrote in September, was one stadium and three years of measuring; target, he said, is either the lap at the far track or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ target I remember is the mark measured in the programme, which closed in 1996 and is still measured as the quietest in the stadium. A ⑩ target, my mother said in 1998, is the only mark that improves by being measured; every target, she said, is an aim that has agreed to look like a mark. She said the aim was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 目标；靶子（指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 目标；靶子（指那个目标本身，与小小的号码布相对）
C. 固定搭配：set the target 设定这一个目标
D. n. 目标；靶子（指留给孩子们数的那一圈）
E. n. 目标之事（抽象总称，指一处体育场的目标之事）
F. n. 目标；靶子（指秩序册里写到、被测量的那一个）
G. n. 目标、追求（指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 追求（抽象总称，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: set the target that no trainer in the stadium would have measured
The target, meaning the mark itself and not the bib
the target at the far track

answers.why: set the target 意为“设定这一个目标”，1989 年那位运动员把体育场里没有一位陪练肯测量的一个目标做了一遍。
target 意为“目标；靶子”，指那个目标本身而不是小小的号码布，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被测量。
target 意为“目标；靶子”，指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一块小小的号码布。
target 意为“目标；靶子”，指最远那条跑道的留给孩子们数的那一圈，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
target 意为“目标、追求”，指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个追求就是那件事的全部。
target 意为“追求”，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个目标，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
target 意为“目标；靶子”，指秩序册里写到、被测量的那一个，到 1994 年这一个成了秩序册里的一行。
target 意为“目标之事”，运动员九月写道，整件事的目标之事是一处体育场和三个年份的测量。
target 意为“目标；靶子”，我记得的是秩序册里测量过的那一个，1996 年跑完了，至今仍被说成体育场里最安静的一个。
target 为抽象总称，母亲 1998 年说，目标是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的目标。
